Stay away from this business!!!
Aug 2026 • Family
I rarely leave reviews like this, but this experience went far beyond receiving a poorly prepared pizza.

I ordered a half pepperoni and half chicken pesto pizza through Grab and paid extra for additional chicken and cheese. Instead of putting the extra chicken on the chicken pesto half, a large amount of it was placed directly on top of the pepperoni half and covered in red sauce. This completely changed the taste of the pepperoni pizza. I couldn't even move the chicken to the pesto side because it was already covered in the red sauce.

Mistakes happen. What turned this into a terrible experience was how the restaurant handled a simple complaint.

When I contacted them, rather than simply acknowledging that putting the extra chicken on the chicken pesto half would have made sense, I was repeatedly told that I should have specified where I wanted the chicken and that I needed to “be clear” next time.

I understand that their ordering system may technically apply an extra topping to the entire pizza. But someone physically prepared a pizza that was HALF PEPPERONI and HALF CHICKEN PESTO. It shouldn't require special instructions to recognize that extra chicken logically belongs with the chicken pesto rather than being piled onto a pepperoni pizza.

I eventually asked for the name of the person I was communicating with. Instead of simply providing a name, I received this response:

“Since you asked for name, I guess you want to bring this further. You're welcome to come and have a chat if you want.”

That was the point where a pizza complaint became genuinely uncomfortable.

Why would a customer need to “come and have a chat” because they asked for the name of the person handling their complaint? I found the wording unnecessarily confrontational and intimidating. To be clear, I am not claiming that an explicit threat was made. I am stating exactly what was said and how the interaction made me feel.

The restaurant eventually offered to remake the pizza. I simply asked them to resend the correctly prepared pizza. They told me it would be ready in 15 minutes and instructed me to arrange pickup.

I explained that I had already paid for an incorrectly prepared delivery and shouldn't have to make transportation arrangements to correct their mistake.

They then asked me for my residential address and a Vietnamese phone number for the driver. I provided my address but explained that I don't have a Vietnamese phone number. Their response?

“So come and pick up.”

At that point, I was done.

I reported the entire situation to Grab and provided documentation. Grab took the complaint seriously and issued a FULL REFUND of the 460,200 VND order.

That should tell you how differently this situation could have been handled.

This never needed to become an argument. The restaurant could simply have said: “Sorry about that. We understand what happened. We'll correct it.”

Instead, a straightforward complaint about misplaced toppings turned into defensiveness, blame being placed on the customer, an invitation to “come and have a chat,” and ultimately Grab having to resolve the matter.

The pizza mistake itself would never have caused me to write a review this serious. Restaurants make mistakes every day. How a business responds when a customer raises a legitimate problem tells you far more about that business than the original mistake.

Grab handled the situation professionally. Unfortunately, Motor City Detroit Style Pizza Da Nang did not.

I have screenshots documenting the entire conversation and have described the interaction as accurately as possible so other customers can make their own judgment.

One bad pizza can be forgiven.

Bad customer service is much harder to swallow.

Lastly.. WAY OVERPRICED!!!
